## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Invoking the TTS function of the Volumio Lovelace Card produces the following error:

> Failed to call service tts/google_translate_say. Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)

All other functions of the Volumio Card seem to work correctly (although there are some display issues with the prev/next buttons).

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 2021.1.4
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): Unknown
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Home Assistant OS 5.10
- Integration causing this issue: Volumio
- Link to integration documentation on our website: [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/volumio/](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/volumio/)

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
# Text to speech

  - platform: google_translate
```

Hi,

I have been looking at this briefly. Here are some of my findings:
1. Volumio integration expects media_id to be json. It uses json internally because it sends commands to volumio via REST.  
2. Volumio is not able to play remote (static) contents via api. It offers playback for dlna and local files (volumio mounts), spotify and webradio. (webradio service may be used for remote content, but it plays the file in a loop)
3. The good news is, volumio uses mpd. Volumio integration could use mpd client library to enable TTS.

I would like to implement it but I am not sure about the expectations.
- Should the current playback stop and only playback TTS result?
- Should the current playback pause for the TTS playback?
- Should TTS result be inserted in the current playback queue (not sure if that is possible)?

I prefer to pause current playback but other implementations like sonos replace the current queue. Please give feedback :-).

@schnabel I think option b would be preferable...

- If no media is playing: just play TTS content
- If media is playing: pause media, play TTS, un-pause media

Assuming that's what you meant?

@schnabel @fraserp 
Maybe it is possible to play TTS without pausing while playing music only by turning it down to e.g. 30% as it is in android with the use of a mixer?

@fraserp Thank you for the feedback. Yes that is what I meant.
At the moment I think about splitting up the solution like the [sonos](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sonos/#service-sonossnapshot) implementation does. That way I could keep the current fix small and we do not have to wait for the [pyvolumio](https://github.com/OnFreund/PyVolumio/issues/4) pull request.

> @schnabel @fraserp Maybe it is possible to play TTS without pausing while playing music only by turning it down to e.g. 30% as it is in android with the use of a mixer?

@eWuPi That would be a cool feature, but as far as I know it will not be possible with volumio. Volumio only plays one item at the time. It is based on [mpd](https://www.musicpd.org/) which does not offer such a feature :-(

I guess they are busy with the volumio 3 stuff. If I find the time I will get in touch with @OnFreund next week to see if we move the code to pyvolumio.

review_comments: The code owner should preferably approve this before we add it. It's unconventional to use two different interfaces and libraries for the same service.

I have to admit I'm not a big fan of this. Volumio has a public API, and I believe that MPD is an implementation detail. Do we know the consequences of calling MPD directly? Is this guaranteed to always be around?

At the very least, I would say this should be encapsulated within PyVolumio, but I think a better approach is to try to add support in Volumio directly - it's also an open source project, and they accept PRs.
Another thought - if we have the URL, can't we call the Volumio API to get the item, and then use that to play?

I would definitely prefer to do it with the volumio api. I have been trying to find a way to do so, but as far as I know neigther REST nor websocket/socketio api offer a way to do it. I have asked [here](https://community.volumio.org/t/playing-remote-music-content/50781) but did not get an answer yet. I would not call mpd an implementation detail. It is the core to play all the music except for spotify as you can see [here](https://volumio.github.io/docs/Development_How_To/System_Architecture.html).
Moving the code to pyvolumio might be a good idea.

The fact that it has an MPD emulation interface is reassuring, but this still doesn't feel right. My first suggestion would be to try to contribute to Volumio API with the missing functionality, and only if that doesn't work for some reason, move the code to PyVolumio.

It is not an emulation interface. It is MPD that is run by volumio.
Nevertheless it would be good if volumio would be able to play remote content, so I will keep on trying with a feature request there. Unfortunately I am not a nodejs coder so I cannot contribute the functionality and it not just an API patch (I think).

> It is not an emulation interface. It is MPD that is run by volumio.

The link you sent shows an MPD Emulation interface, and that's more important than running on MPD (because it means the interface is more likely to be stay around and be supported).

@OnFreund I should have looked closer before my last answer :-). Of course you are right, there is a mpd emulation interface.
With the link above I was trying to point to the 'Music Controllers' and 'Music Services' section.
Anyway, knowing the emulation exists makes me comfortable adding this to PyVolumio. My preference is still for this to be supported by Volumio directly, though.
